data.title: Decapeptide lotion (e.g. Melbild/Melgain)
data.summary: VIII Pigmentary / depigmenting · Synthetic decapeptide (repigmenting agent) — a bFGF-related peptide
data.body:
_Topicals · VIII Pigmentary / depigmenting_

**Class:** Synthetic decapeptide (repigmenting agent) — a bFGF-related peptide

## Mechanism of action
- Mimics a part of basic fibroblast growth factor (bFGF), a natural mitogen for melanocytes
- Stimulates melanocyte proliferation and migration, and melanogenesis
- Used to support repigmentation (not depigmentation)

## Indications in dermatology & STI
- Stable vitiligo (localised and generalised) — adjunct to phototherapy, topical steroids or tacrolimus
- Children and face (steroid-sparing)

## Dose & formulations
- Apply once daily to patches; many protocols advise sun exposure (morning) or NB-UVB after application
- Response takes 3–6 months

## Adverse effects
- Mild itching, burning, redness; generally very well tolerated

## Contraindications
- Hypersensitivity

## Pregnancy & lactation
Insufficient data; low absorption.

## Viva points
- A repigmenting peptide, not a depigmenting agent — classified here with pigmentary agents
- bFGF-mimicking decapeptide → melanocyte proliferation
- Evidence is modest (Indian studies)

_Sources: Khopkar (Topical immunomodulators — basic fibroblast growth factor decapeptide). Facts summarised in our own words; Wolverton followed where books differ._
